name: sharpen_program
description: Program that rebuilds the object on the sharpened grid [Derived-Programs]
notes: a213. The fourth thing a probe produces, beside sharpen_df / sharpen_description / sharpen_explanation. a215 [Sharpen-Pin]: sharpen() now writes that outcome onto the object's own program/note/hints as it finishes, so this is that program RENDERED TO READ (spread layout, trailer left in, since here the trailer is the payload) rather than a re-derivation. Which of four to reach for: this for text to read or share, program for the one-line stamp, hints for the settings alone, note for the verdict alone. Grid moved -> hints{log2=...; bs=...} and nothing else, the hints being the record. Grid confirmed -> note{sharpen: grid confirmed, no change} and DELIBERATELY no hints: pinning a grid the automatic selector would have picked anyway is noise in a program someone will read and share, and implies the selector is not trusted; the note records that the audit ran, which is what saves running it twice. execute=False that recommends a move -> a note carrying the recommendation, since the object is still on its original grid. '' before sharpen runs. A grid the caller pinned via build(program, log2=20) is not in the text and not visible to the probe, so it is not pinned either.

name: pnl_program
description: Program that wraps the object in a P&L [Derived-Programs]
notes: a213. pnl NAME_PnL <premium> less <engine> less <expense>. Aggregate INLINES its own body (self-contained: builds anywhere, nothing registered first) stripped of its trailer, which the wrapping pnl now owns; the aggregate's own `as` label becomes the engine label, which names the P&L's loss leg. Portfolio REFERENCES (less port.NAME) because the grammar has no inline portfolio engine, so it resolves against the knowledge base build put it in. Premium is `inherit premium` when the exposure states one, else expected loss (the empirical est_m, so the realized ratio is exactly the one asked for) over loss_ratio=0.70; expense_ratio=0.25 of premium, 0 omitting the clause rather than writing a zero. Both defaults are conventions and sit in the signature.

name: reins_program
description: Program that rebuilds the object with a cession added [Derived-Programs]
notes: a213. Takes one cession clause per tier ('occurrence net of 500 xs 500'), or a sequence for both. The SLOT is the point: an occurrence cession sits before the frequency clause and an aggregate cession after it, so neither can be appended to the text; the clause is parsed in a throwaway carrier, lifted as spec keys and re-rendered, never spliced. Authoritative for its own tier only, so an occurrence clause leaves the aggregate program alone. SELF-CONTAINED by design: `agg NEW agg.OLD occurrence net of ...` is grammatical and is the obvious first idea, but agg.OLD resolves only against a knowledge base that holds OLD, so the text would build in the session that made it and nowhere else, and a shared server would write every user's builds into one store. No Portfolio: a portfolio has no cession clause, its units do.

name: sharpen
description: Probe the (bs log2) neighbourhood and move to a better grid
notes: a192 [Sharpen-Grid-Probe]. update CHOOSES a grid from the analytic moments before any FFT runs; sharpen AUDITS that choice after, re-updating on neighbouring cells and scoring each with validation_score. a193: a row per log2, and within each a LINE SEARCH out from the current bucket (bs doubled until the score stops improving, then halved likewise, capped at bs_limit=16 each way), so a grid wrong by two orders of magnitude is reachable in one call instead of three. a194: SELECTION is the best score among cells that do NOT grow log2 (never make the caller pay more than they already are); log2 grows by one only when nothing at the current size or smaller reaches good_enough and something larger does, so the log2+1 row is computed lazily and usually not at all. min_gain RETIRED, good_enough is the only judgment knob. log2_cap default 24 -> 20. A discrete severity whose atoms are a whole number of buckets has its bucket PINNED (coarser scatters the atoms, finer wastes grid): only log2 is probed, detected via Aggregate._severity_lattice, gcd across units for a Portfolio. a195: SOUNDNESS GATE. A cell with a genuine deficit (mass off the top of the grid, threshold VALIDATION_NOISE, the level at which DefectiveDistributionWarning fires) is disqualified while any clean cell survives. A gate not a score term: score terms each divide by their own validation tolerance and a deficit has none, and far-tail mass is negligible for the first three moments while being decisive for tail pricing, so the score is blind to it. Because the affordability test now runs over clean cells, a deficit is also a reason to grow log2, which is its cure. The probe gate is now at target AND sound"
column18: so a good-moments/lost-mass grid is no longer waved through. Two gates off one number good_enough (default 0.5
column19: in validation-tolerance units): a grid already at or under it is not probed at all (good_enough=0 forces the probe)
column20: and among cells that meet it the SMALLEST log2 wins
column21: so a probe never quietly doubles the grid for a marginal gain. execute=False restores the original grid AND the sev_calc/discretization_calc/normalize/padding settings a bare re-update would reset. Portfolio probes with add_exa=False and scores the TOTAL only. No BivariateAggregate (quadratic) and no PnL (its ledger snapshots the source atoms; a pnl gets sharpening through its engine pre-construction). a215 [Sharpen-Pin]: the probe now PINS its outcome onto the object's own program / note / hints as it finishes
column22: so the three agree and build(ob.program) reproduces the sharpened object; a moved grid becomes hints{log2=...; bs=...}
column23: a confirmed one a note{sharpen: ...} and no hints. Sharpen's own sentence is namespaced and REPLACED on a re-probe
column24: never stacked. A no-op for an object with no program (built in Python) or one whose program cannot be re-parsed; neither is worth failing a probe over."
